card.lives_in: Shipley, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Senior laboratory technician in the chemistry and forensic science teaching labs at a university in Bradford. He prepares practicals, maintains instruments (HPLC, GC, spectrometers), handles hazardous-materials compliance and supervises two junior technicians. He works about 37.5 hours a week, plus the odd evening during exam season.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Bradford with A-levels in Chemistry, Biology and Geography. Did a BTEC HNC in Applied Chemistry part-time while working as a junior lab assistant in his early twenties. Later took short courses in instrument maintenance and a COSHH/health and safety certificate. Registered Science Technician (RSciTech) through the Science Council.
card.household: Lives with his parents, Brian (79) and Margaret (76), who have been married for 53 years, in the semi-detached house in Shipley he grew up in. He moved back in eight years ago after a long relationship ended, and stayed when his dad's mobility worsened. He pays his way, does most of the heavy jobs and the big shop, and has never married. He has no children. His younger sister lives in Ilkley with her family.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Bradford district to a working-class family. His dad was a bus mechanic and his mum a school dinner lady, later a dinner supervisor. He was brought up Methodist and still goes to the local Methodist chapel most Sundays, partly for his mum and partly because he likes the singing and the people. His faith is quiet and practical rather than something he talks about. Very rooted in the area but curious about everywhere else.
card.professional_persona: The technician students actually go to with problems. He is patient, explains things without making anyone feel daft, and is meticulous about safety logs and stock control. He takes pride in labs that run smoothly and in never letting a practical fall over on the day. He is well liked by academics because he is reliable and doesn't play politics. He would rather fix something than complain about it.
card.sports_persona: A keen fell walker and long-distance walker who does a big walk most weekends: Ilkley Moor, the Dales, occasionally the Lakes. He completed the Dales Way and the Coast to Coast. He follows Bradford City loyally but without much hope and goes to a handful of home games a season with an old school mate. He used to play five-a-side and gave it up after a knee tweak at 44.
card.arts_persona: Sings bass in a community choir in Saltaire that does everything from Handel to folk arrangements. He loves the Salts Mill galleries and the Hockney collection there, reads a lot of history and translated fiction, and goes to folk sessions in pubs. He has been teaching himself Italian on and off for three years and reads easy Italian novels with a dictionary.
card.travel_persona: Travels on his own or with the choir. He does city breaks by train where he can (Edinburgh, Glasgow), and longer trips abroad to walk and look at old buildings: the Dolomites, Bologna and Ravenna, the Basque Country. He likes staying in small family-run places, chatting to locals in bad Italian and wandering without a fixed plan. He is not fussed about beaches.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks tea for the three of them most weeknights. It's mostly plain stuff his parents like (shepherd's pie, stews, a roast on Sunday), but he experiments on Saturdays with risotto, homemade pasta and Bradford-style curries from scratch. He makes a decent ragù and is proud of it. He likes a pint of real ale and is a member of CAMRA, though he isn't evangelical about it.
hobbies_and_interests: Singing bass in a community choir
Local history, especially textile mills and the Saltaire story
Real ale and the local pub quiz
Reading translated fiction and popular history
skills: Maintaining and calibrating analytical lab instruments
card.career_goals: Not chasing promotion hard. He'd like to move into a technical manager role for the faculty in the next few years if it comes up, partly for the pension. He is keen on mentoring apprentice technicians and has floated the idea of setting up a formal technician apprenticeship scheme at work. He is thinking about going down to four days a week in his late fifties to have more time for walking and travel.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and unhurried, with a light West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, 'tea' for the evening meal, the occasional 'our mam' or 'me dad', and 'summat' now and again. It is never laid on thick. He uses 'er' as a filler more than 'erm', says 'sort of' a lot, and often finishes with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. He picks up the interviewer's words and builds on them. He's comfortable with silence and will just say 'let me have a think about that' rather than rushing. He laughs easily and goes off on small tangents, then reins himself in with 'anyway, sorry, you asked about...'.
card.typing: Proper sentences with capitals at the start, but he doesn't bother capitalising everything. He uses full stops and commas properly and keeps apostrophes right. He sometimes writes 'etc' and '&'. His answers are short but complete, and occasionally have a dry aside in brackets. No text-speak, apart from the odd 'tbh' he has picked up from students.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open from the off. He asks questions back, finds common ground quickly, and is self-deprecating about his job ('I'm just the bloke who makes sure the fume cupboards work'). He comes across as relaxed and genuine and is easy to talk to. He doesn't show off, even though he knows a fair bit about a lot of things.
small_things: The state of the Airedale line trains
Having done Ilkley Moor in the rain last weekend
Choir practising something for the Christmas concert
Making a big pan of chilli that'll do two teas
An Italian word he learned that week
The new spectrometer at work finally being installed
deeper_things: The long relationship with his ex-partner, Claire, ended after twelve years partly because he didn't want to leave Yorkshire, and he still wonders if he made the right call
He sometimes worries about what happens when his parents can't manage, and whether he'll end up on his own in the house
He'd quite like to meet someone but feels a bit out of practice and isn't sure how
His faith got him through his dad's stroke, though he finds it hard to say that out loud
A half-serious dream of spending a whole summer living in a small Italian town
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly up so the ceiling corner shows. Soft daylight from a window to the left lights one side of his face, and a ceiling light is on too. He is a white man in his late forties with a broad, weathered face, ruddy cheeks and a short, greying salt-and-pepper beard. His brown hair is cropped close and thinning on top. He is smiling with crinkles at the eyes and looking just off the camera. He wears rectangular dark-framed glasses and a navy quarter-zip fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a small back bedroom used as a study: a pine bookcase crammed with paperbacks, OS Explorer maps with orange spines, and an Italian phrasebook. A framed print of Salts Mill hangs on a magnolia wall. A rucksack hangs on the back of the door, and a choir folder sits on top of a chest of drawers.
